institution.fact: The President appoints the Prime Minister under article 75(1); the official 2024 appointment explains the assessment of majority support in the Lok Sabha. Party chairmanship is not itself that appointment.
institution.gameplay_assumption: New historical party offices are reference/party-only. Fictional party successors require a separately authored and reviewed executive contender grant before the existing government simulation can select their identity for national office. This gate does not add a full constitutional or nomination simulation.

executive_policy.note: Party leadership and national office are separate roles. Calendar references and party chairs never schedule a presidency.

assumptions: All candidate names, biographies, birthdays, appearances and future careers are invented game content. Coincidental resemblance is unintentional.
Name pools are authored examples, not an exhaustive or demographic representation of any country; bilingual and multiethnic populations require further editorial review.
Existing simulation institutions and ideology supply fictional career themes. This does not forecast real institutions or party survival after the research cutoff.
Four stable candidates per party component become eligible after the cutoff, only through actual gameplay succession. No candidate is a scheduled election winner.
Historical gaps before the cutoff remain unfilled; no fictional candidate may be presented as a historical leader.
Names use authored romanized forms; native spellings are not invented.

research.applies_to: Institutional framing only; not evidence for any fictional person or a forecast.
research.fact: Political parties recruit candidates, organize leadership selection, formulate programmes and aggregate interests. Selection institutions differ between parties.

research.applies_to: Parliamentary career archetype example; not a universal constitutional rule.
research.fact: Government and opposition parties have distinct parliamentary roles; party leaders and shadow teams organize parliamentary work.

future_policy.scope: Every current simulation party in POLITIES and D4_POLITIES, including researched coalition components; not every real-world party.

note: Historical references end on 7 September 2026. Fictional successor candidates are available from 8 September 2026 through 2035. Saved incumbents change only through actual campaign events; no historical or future election outcome is scheduled.

portrait.era_note: Observed reference date: 2018-09-26. Approved illustrative appearance interval 2020-01-20 to 2026-01-20 (exclusive), exactly as requested. Born 2 December 1960: the reference file's own Commons description says 'Jagat Prakash Nadda (born 2 December 1960)' (saved in commons-api-endtb-20180926.json, sha256 ee1135d4089095696b7f4f42e540c697155286eb888b7f1f4f75981135410ac1); the registry identity source https://www.mohfw.gov.in/sites/default/files/jagatprakashnadda.pdf is another. General biographical knowledge, not C01 research. Photographed on 26 September 2018, aged 57, as Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare. The window is 2020-01-20 to 2026-01-20 (exclusive), when he is 59 to 65. The photograph is about 1 year 4 months before the window opens and about 7 years 4 months before it closes. The prompt asks for a man of about 59 to 65, only slightly older, with the same black hair, spectacles and black moustache. The 2018 clothing is kept for the whole window as an artistic choice (in-window public dress was often a white kurta-pyjama with a saffron stole). The changed hand pose is an artistic extension. Predates the window. No qualifying in-window photograph exists on Commons: nearly all Nadda files are GODL-India, and the in-window non-GODL files are rejected below. Art availability only: no new office boundary, tenure or historical acceptance. The source precedes the window; age and dress continuity are disclosed artistic choices. Original Adobe RGB source bytes were preserved; no independent image transformation is inferred from file naming or display.

portrait.era_note: Observed reference date: 2019-12-27 or 2019-12-28 (sources disagree). Approved illustrative appearance interval 2015-04-30 to 2024-09-12 (exclusive), exactly as requested. Born 12 August 1952 (English Wikipedia lead, saved in D:/spheres-scratch/in-cast/assemble/enwiki-birthdates-intro.json; general biographical knowledge, not C01 research; the registry gives only his death on 2024-09-12). The photograph of 27 or 28 December 2019 is 1,702 or 1,703 days after the window start (2015-04-30) and 1,720 or 1,719 days before its last day (2024-09-11), almost exactly at the midpoint and a few days before the leadership-production boundary 2020-01-01. He is 67 in the photo and 62 to 72 in the window. The prompt targets about 67 with the same silver hair and glasses. Codex may split at 2020-01-01; the same reference fits both halves. No CC0/CC BY/CC BY-SA photograph of him as the sole subject was found nearer the window ends. The in-window government photographs are GODL-India, which is not on the list, or a press handout. Art availability only: no new office boundary, tenure or historical acceptance. The December 27/28, 2019 source-day ambiguity remains. One midpoint portrait represents the wider 2015–2024 artistic interval.
